    2. MULTI-HEAD ATTENTION
       - Use case: Transform
```python
    2. MULTI-HEAD ATTENTION
       - Use case: Transformers, parallel attention patterns
       - Complexity: O(N²·D)
       
    3. CROSS-ATTENTION
       - Use case: Encoder-decoder models, seq2seq
       - Complexity: O(N·M·D)
       
    4. SCALED DOT-PRODUCT ATTENTION
       - Use case: Core building block for transformers
       - Complexity: O(N²·D)
       
    5. ADDITIVE ATTENTION (Bahdanau)
       - Use case: RNN-based seq2seq, machine translation
       - Complexity: O(N·D·H)
       
    6. MULTIPLICATIVE ATTENTION (Luong)
       - Use case: RNN-based models, alignment
       - Complexity: O(N·D)
       
    7. SPATIAL ATTENTION
       - Use case: Computer vision, image segmentation
       - Complexity: O(H·W·K²)
       
    8. CHANNEL ATTENTION (SE Blocks)
       - Use case: CNNs, feature recalibration
       - Complexity: O(C²/r)
       
    9. CBAM (Channel + Spatial)
       - Use case: Image classification, object detection
       - Complexity: O(H·W·K² + C²/r)
       
    10. NON-LOCAL BLOCKS
        - Use case: Video understanding, long-range dependencies
        - Complexity: O(N²·D)
        
    11. AXIAL ATTENTION
        - Use case: High-resolution images, 3D data
        - Complexity: O(N·√N·D)
        
    12. LINEAR ATTENTION
        - Use case: Very long sequences, efficient transformers
        - Complexity: O(N·D²)
        
    13. SPARSE ATTENTION
        - Use case: Long documents, genomic sequences
        - Complexity: O(N·W·D)
        
    14. LOCAL WINDOW ATTENTION
        - Use case: Vision transformers, sliding windows
        - Complexity: O(N·W·D)
        
    15. GLOBAL CONTEXT ATTENTION
        - Use case: Capturing global information efficiently
        - Complexity: O(N·D)
    
    ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
                              BEST PRACTICES
    ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
    
    CHOOSING THE RIGHT ATTENTION:
    
    For NLP Tasks:
    • Short sequences (< 512): Multi-Head Attention
    • Long sequences (> 2048): Linear or Sparse Attention
    • Translation: Cross-Attention between encoder-decoder
    • Autoregressive: Self-Attention with causal masking
    
    For Computer Vision:
    • Image classification: CBAM or SE Blocks
    • Object detection: Non-Local Blocks
    • Segmentation: Spatial Attention
    • High-res images: Axial Attention
    • Vision Transformers: Multi-Head with Local Windows
    
    For Video/3D:
    • Video understanding: Non-Local Blocks
    • 3D medical imaging: Axial Attention
    • Temporal modeling: Self-Attention on time dimension
    
    PERFORMANCE OPTIMIZATION:
    
    1. Memory Efficiency:
       ✓ Use gradient checkpointing for deep models
       ✓ Enable mixed precision training (FP16)
       ✓ Use chunked processing for long sequences
       ✓ Cache key/value pairs during inference
    
    2. Speed Optimization:
       ✓ Use Flash Attention (PyTorch 2.0+)
       ✓ Fuse QKV projections
       ✓ Use efficient attention patterns (sparse/local)
       ✓ Batch operations when possible
    
    3. Model Quality:
       ✓ Use layer normalization before attention
       ✓ Add residual connections
       ✓ Apply dropout to attention weights
       ✓ Use relative position encodings
    
    COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID:
    
    ✗ Don't forget to scale attention scores (divide by √d_k)
    ✗ Don't use softmax on masked positions (use -inf before softmax)
    ✗ Don't ignore numerical stability (add epsilon where needed)
    ✗ Don't forget dropout during training
    ✗ Don't mix up query/key dimensions in cross-attention
    
    DEBUGGING TIPS:
    
    • Check attention weight distributions (should sum to 1)
    • Visualize attention patterns to verify behavior
    • Monitor gradient norms (watch for vanishing/exploding)
    • Verify mask shapes match attention score shapes
    • Test with small inputs first
    
    ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
                            IMPLEMENTATION CHECKLIST
    ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
    
    Before deploying your attention mechanism:
    
    □ Proper input/output shape handling
    □ Numerical stability (scaling, epsilon values)
    □ Mask handling (padding, causal, etc.)
    □ Dropout applied correctly
    □ Residual connections where appropriate
    □ Layer normalization placement
    □ Gradient checkpointing for memory
    □ Mixed precision compatibility
    □ Efficient batching
    □ Proper initialization
    
    ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
    """
    print(summary)

class AttentionVisualizer:

        """

        """

            elif attention_weights.dim() == 3:

            else:

        # Entropy analysis

            axes[1, 1].set_title('Attention Entropy per Query Position')
            axes[1, 1].set_xlabel('Query Position')

            axes[1, 1].axhline(entropies.mean(), color='r',

        plt.tight_layout()
        plt.show()


class AttentionProfiler:
    """
    Profiling utilities for analyzing attention mechanism performance.
    """
    
    @staticmethod
    def profile_memory(attention_module, input_tensor, num_runs=10):
        """
        Profile memory usage of an attention module.
        
        Args:
            attention_module: Attention module to profile
            input_tensor: Input tensor
            num_runs: Number of profiling runs
            
        Returns:
            Dictionary with memory statistics
        """
        import gc
        
        # Clear cache
        if torch.cuda.is_available():
            torch.cuda.empty_cache()
            torch.cuda.reset_peak_memory_stats()
        
        gc.collect()
        
        # Warmup
        with torch.no_grad():
            _ = attention_module(input_tensor)
        
        # Profile
        memory_stats = {
            'allocated': [],
            'reserved': [],
            'peak': []
        }
        
        for _ in range(num_runs):
            if torch.cuda.is_available():
                torch.cuda.empty_cache()
                torch.cuda.reset_peak_memory_stats()
            
            gc.collect()
            
            with torch.no_grad():
                _ = attention_module(input_tensor)
            
            if torch.cuda.is_available():
                memory_stats['allocated'].append(
                    torch.cuda.memory_allocated() / 1024**2  # MB
                )
                memory_stats['reserved'].append(
                    torch.cuda.memory_reserved() / 1024**2  # MB
                )
                memory_stats['peak'].append(
                    torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated() / 1024**2  # MB
                )
        
        # Calculate statistics
        results = {}
        for key, values in memory_stats.items():
            if values:
                results[f'{key}_mean_mb'] = np.mean(values)
                results[f'{key}_std_mb'] = np.std(values)
                results[f'{key}_max_mb'] = np.max(values)
        
        return results
    
    @staticmethod
    def profile_speed(attention_module, input_tensor, num_warmup=5, num_runs=50):
        """
        Profile execution speed of an attention module.
        
        Args:
            attention_module: Attention module to profile
            input_tensor: Input tensor
            num_warmup: Number of warmup iterations
            num_runs: Number of profiling runs
            
        Returns:
            Dictionary with timing statistics
        """
        import time
        
        # Warmup
        for _ in range(num_warmup):
            with torch.no_grad():
                _ = attention_module(input_tensor)
        
        # Synchronize if using CUDA
        if torch.cuda.is_available():
            torch.cuda.synchronize()
        
        # Profile
        times = []
        for _ in range(num_runs):
            start = time.perf_counter()
            
            with torch.no_grad():
                _ = attention_module(input_tensor)
            
            if torch.cuda.is_available():
                torch.cuda.synchronize()
            
            end = time.perf_counter()
            times.append((end - start) * 1000)  # Convert to ms
        
        return {
            'mean_ms': np.mean(times),
            'std_ms': np.std(times),
            'min_ms': np.min(times),
            'max_ms': np.max(times),
            'median_ms': np.median(times),
            'p95_ms': np.percentile(times, 95),
            'p99_ms': np.percentile(times, 99)
        }
    
    @staticmethod
    def compare_mechanisms(mechanisms_dict, input_tensor, 
                          profile_memory=True, profile_speed=True):
        """
        Compare multiple attention mechanisms.
        
        Args:
            mechanisms_dict: Dict of {name: module} to compare
            input_tensor: Input tensor
            profile_memory: Whether to profile memory
            profile_speed: Whether to profile speed
            
        Returns:
            Comparison results
        """
        results = {}
        
        print("\n" + "=" * 80)
        print("ATTENTION MECHANISM COMPARISON")
        print("=" * 80)
        
        for name, module in mechanisms_dict.items():
            print(f"\nProfiling {name}...")
            results[name] = {}
            
            if profile_speed:
                speed_stats = AttentionProfiler.profile_speed(module, input_tensor)
                results[name]['speed'] = speed_stats
                print(f"  Speed: {speed_stats['mean_ms']:.3f} ± {speed_stats['std_ms']:.3f} ms")
            
            if profile_memory and torch.cuda.is_available():
                memory_stats = AttentionProfiler.profile_memory(module, input_tensor)
                results[name]['memory'] = memory_stats
                print(f"  Memory: {memory_stats.get('peak_mean_mb', 0):.2f} MB (peak)")
        
        print("\n" + "=" * 80)
        
        return results


class AttentionAnalyzer:
    """
    Tools for analyzing attention patterns and behaviors.
    """
    
    @staticmethod
    def compute_attention_entropy(attention_weights):
        """
        Compute entropy of attention distributions.
        Higher entropy = more uniform attention, Lower = more focused.
        
        Args:
            attention_weights: Attention weights tensor
            
        Returns:
            Entropy values
        """
        epsilon = 1e-10
        if isinstance(attention_weights, torch.Tensor):
            weights = attention_weights.detach()
            entropy = -torch.sum(weights * torch.log(weights + epsilon), dim=-1)
        else:
            weights = attention_weights
            entropy = -np.sum(weights * np.log(weights + epsilon), axis=-1)
        
        return entropy
    
    @staticmethod
    def compute_attention_sparsity(attention_weights, threshold=0.01):
        """
        Compute sparsity of attention (fraction of near-zero weights).
        
        Args:
            attention_weights: Attention weights tensor
            threshold: Threshold below which weights are considered zero
            
        Returns:
            Sparsity ratio (0 to 1)
        """
        if isinstance(attention_weights, torch.Tensor):
            weights = attention_weights.detach()
            sparsity = (weights < threshold).float().mean()
        else:
            weights = attention_weights
            sparsity = (weights < threshold).mean()
        
        return sparsity
    
    @staticmethod
    def find_attended_positions(attention_weights, top_k=5):
        """
        Find the most attended positions for each query.
        
        Args:
            attention_weights: Attention weights (seq_len, seq_len)
            top_k: Number of top positions to return
            
        Returns:
            Indices and values of top-k attended positions
        """
        if isinstance(attention_weights, torch.Tensor):
            weights = attention_weights.detach()
            values, indices = torch.topk(weights, k=top_k, dim=-1)
            return indices.cpu().numpy(), values.cpu().numpy()
        else:
            indices = np.argsort(attention_weights, axis=-1)[..., -top_k:]
            values = np.take_along_axis(attention_weights, indices, axis=-1)
            return indices, values
    
    @staticmethod
    def analyze_attention_pattern(attention_weights):
        """
        Comprehensive analysis of attention patterns.
        
        Args:
            attention_weights: Attention weights tensor
            
        Returns:
            Dictionary with analysis results
        """
        if isinstance(attention_weights, torch.Tensor):
            weights = attention_weights.detach().cpu().numpy()
        else:
            weights = attention_weights
        
        analysis = {
            'shape': weights.shape,
            'mean': float(np.mean(weights)),
            'std': float(np.std(weights)),
            'min
```python
            'min': float(np.min(weights)),
            'max': float(np.max(weights)),
            'entropy_mean': float(np.mean(AttentionAnalyzer.compute_attention_entropy(weights))),
            'sparsity': float(AttentionAnalyzer.compute_attention_sparsity(weights)),
        }
        
        # Check for common patterns
        if weights.ndim >= 2:
            # Diagonal dominance (self-attention to same position)
            diag_strength = np.mean(np.diag(weights)) if weights.shape[-2] == weights.shape[-1] else 0
            analysis['diagonal_strength'] = float(diag_strength)
            
            # Local vs global attention
            seq_len = weights.shape[-1]
            if seq_len > 3:
                # Local: attention to nearby positions
                local_window = 3
                local_mask = np.zeros_like(weights)
                for i in range(weights.shape[-2]):
                    start = max(0, i - local_window)
                    end = min(seq_len, i + local_window + 1)
                    local_mask[..., i, start:end] = 1
                
                local_attention = np.sum(weights * local_mask) / np.sum(local_mask)
                analysis['local_attention_ratio'] = float(local_attention)
            
            # Uniformity (how uniform is the attention distribution)
            uniformity = 1.0 / (1.0 + analysis['std'])
            analysis['uniformity'] = float(uniformity)
        
        return analysis


# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
#                    ADVANCED ATTENTION VARIANTS
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

class RelativePositionAttention(nn.Module):
    """
    Multi-Head Attention with relative position encodings.
    Improves generalization to different sequence lengths.
    
    Args:
        embed_dim: Embedding dimension
        num_heads: Number of attention heads
        max_relative_position: Maximum relative position to consider
        dropout: Dropout probability
    """
    def __init__(self, embed_dim, num_heads=8, max_relative_position=128, dropout=0.1):
        super(RelativePositionAttention, self).__init__()
        
        assert embed_dim % num_heads == 0
        
        self.embed_dim = embed_dim
        self.num_heads = num_heads
        self.head_dim = embed_dim // num_heads
        self.max_relative_position = max_relative_position
        self.scale = math.sqrt(self.head_dim)
        
        # Q, K, V projections
        self.qkv_proj = nn.Linear(embed_dim, 3 * embed_dim)
        self.out_proj = nn.Linear(embed_dim, embed_dim)
        
        # Relative position embeddings
        self.relative_position_k = nn.Embedding(
            2 * max_relative_position + 1, self.head_dim
        )
        self.relative_position_v = nn.Embedding(
            2 * max_relative_position + 1, self.head_dim
        )
        
        self.dropout = nn.Dropout(dropout)
        
    def _get_relative_positions(self, seq_len):
        """Generate relative position indices."""
        range_vec = torch.arange(seq_len)
        range_mat = range_vec.unsqueeze(0).expand(seq_len, seq_len)
        distance_mat = range_mat - range_mat.transpose(0, 1)
        
        # Clip to max relative position
        distance_mat_clipped = torch.clamp(
            distance_mat,
            -self.max_relative_position,
            self.max_relative_position
        )
        
        # Shift to be >= 0
        final_mat = distance_mat_clipped + self.max_relative_position
        
        return final_mat
    
    def forward(self, x, mask=None):
        """
        Args:
            x: Input tensor (B, L, D)
            mask: Optional attention mask
            
        Returns:
            Output tensor (B, L, D)
        """
        B, L, D = x.shape
        
        # Generate Q, K, V
        qkv = self.qkv_proj(x)
        qkv = qkv.reshape(B, L, 3, self.num_heads, self.head_dim)
        qkv = qkv.permute(2, 0, 3, 1, 4)
        Q, K, V = qkv[0], qkv[1], qkv[2]  # (B, H, L, D)
        
        # Content-based attention
        content_scores = torch.matmul(Q, K.transpose(-2, -1)) / self.scale
        
        # Relative position-based attention
        relative_positions = self._get_relative_positions(L).to(x.device)
        relative_k = self.relative_position_k(relative_positions)  # (L, L, D)
        
        # Compute position-based scores
        # Q: (B, H, L, D), relative_k: (L, L, D)
        position_scores = torch.einsum('bhld,lrd->bhlr', Q, relative_k) / self.scale
        
        # Combine content and position scores
        scores = content_scores + position_scores
        
        # Apply mask if provided
        if mask is not None:
            scores = scores.masked_fill(mask == 0, float('-inf'))
        
        # Apply softmax
        attn_weights = F.softmax(scores, dim=-1)
        attn_weights = self.dropout(attn_weights)
        
        # Apply attention to values (content)
        content_output = torch.matmul(attn_weights, V)
        
        # Apply attention to values (position)
        relative_v = self.relative_position_v(relative_positions)
        position_output = torch.einsum('bhlr,lrd->bhld', attn_weights, relative_v)
        
        # Combine outputs
        attn_output = content_output + position_output
        
        # Reshape and project
        attn_output = attn_output.transpose(1, 2).contiguous()
        attn_output = attn_output.reshape(B, L, D)
        output = self.out_proj(attn_output)
        
        return output


class RotaryPositionAttention(nn.Module):
    """
    Multi-Head Attention with Rotary Position Embeddings (RoPE).
    More efficient than absolute position encodings.
    
    Args:
        embed_dim: Embedding dimension
        num_heads: Number of attention heads
        max_seq_len: Maximum sequence length
        dropout: Dropout probability
    """
    def __init__(self, embed_dim, num_heads=8, max_seq_len=2048, dropout=0.1):
        super(RotaryPositionAttention, self).__init__()
        
        assert embed_dim % num_heads == 0
        
        self.embed_dim = embed_dim
        self.num_heads = num_heads
        self.head_dim = embed_dim // num_heads
        self.scale = math.sqrt(self.head_dim)
        
        # Q, K, V projections
        self.qkv_proj = nn.Linear(embed_dim, 3 * embed_dim)
        self.out_proj = nn.Linear(embed_dim, embed_dim)
        
        self.dropout = nn.Dropout(dropout)
        
        # Precompute rotary embeddings
        self.register_buffer(
            'cos_cached',
            self._compute_cos_sin_cache(max_seq_len, self.head_dim)[0]
        )
        self.register_buffer(
            'sin_cached',
            self._compute_cos_sin_cache(max_seq_len, self.head_dim)[1]
        )
    
    def _compute_cos_sin_cache(self, seq_len, dim):
        """Precompute cos and sin for rotary embeddings."""
        inv_freq = 1.0 / (10000 ** (torch.arange(0, dim, 2).float() / dim))
        t = torch.arange(seq_len).type_as(inv_freq)
        freqs = torch.einsum('i,j->ij', t, inv_freq)
        emb = torch.cat((freqs, freqs), dim=-1)
        return emb.cos(), emb.sin()
    
    def _apply_rotary_pos_emb(self, x, cos, sin):
        """Apply rotary position embeddings to input tensor."""
        # x: (B, H, L, D)
        seq_len = x.shape[2]
        cos = cos[:seq_len, :].unsqueeze(0).unsqueeze(0)
        sin = sin[:seq_len, :].unsqueeze(0).unsqueeze(0)
        
        # Rotate
        x1, x2 = x[..., ::2], x[..., 1::2]
        
        # Apply rotation
        rotated = torch.stack([
            x1 * cos - x2 * sin,
            x1 * sin + x2 * cos
        ], dim=-1)
        
        return rotated.flatten(-2)
    
    def forward(self, x, mask=None):
        """
        Args:
            x: Input tensor (B, L, D)
            mask: Optional attention mask
            
        Returns:
            Output tensor (B, L, D)
        """
        B, L, D = x.shape
        
        # Generate Q, K, V
        qkv = self.qkv_proj(x)
        qkv = qkv.reshape(B, L, 3, self.num_heads, self.head_dim)
        qkv = qkv.permute(2, 0, 3, 1, 4)
        Q, K, V = qkv[0], qkv[1], qkv[2]  # (B, H, L, D)
        
        # Apply rotary embeddings to Q and K
        Q = self._apply_rotary_pos_emb(Q, self.cos_cached, self.sin_cached)
        K = self._apply_rotary_pos_emb(K, self.cos_cached, self.sin_cached)
        
        # Compute attention
        scores = torch.matmul(Q, K.transpose(-2, -1)) / self.scale
        
        if mask is not None:
            scores = scores.masked_fill(mask == 0, float('-inf'))
        
        attn_weights = F.softmax(scores, dim=-1)
        attn_weights = self.dropout(attn_weights)
        
        attn_output = torch.matmul(attn_weights, V)
        
        # Reshape and project
        attn_output = attn_output.transpose(1, 2).contiguous()
        attn_output = attn_output.reshape(B, L, D)
        output = self.out_proj(attn_output)
        
        return output


class GatedAttention(nn.Module):
    """
    Gated Attention mechanism with learnable gating for adaptive attention.
    Useful for multi-modal fusion and selective attention.
    
    Args:
        embed_dim: Embedding dimension
        num_heads: Number of attention heads
        dropout: Dropout probability
    """
    def __init__(self, embed_dim, num_heads=8, dropout=0.1):
        super(GatedAttention, self).__init__()
        
        assert embed_dim % num_heads == 0
        
        self.embed_dim = embed_dim
        self.num_heads = num_heads
        self.head_dim = embed_dim // num_heads
        self.scale = math.sqrt(self.head_dim)
        
        # Q, K, V projections
        self.qkv_proj = nn.Linear(embed_dim, 3 * embed_dim)
        self.out_proj = nn.Linear(embed_dim, embed_dim)
        
        # Gating mechanism
        self.gate = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(embed_dim, embed_dim),
            nn.Sigmoid()
        )
        
        self.dropout = nn.Dropout(dropout)
        
    def forward(self, x, mask=None):
        """
        Args:
            x: Input tensor (B, L, D)
            mask: Optional attention mask
            
        Returns:
            Output tensor (B, L, D)
        """
        B, L, D = x.shape
        
        # Compute gate values
        gate_values = self.gate(x)  # (B, L, D)
        
        # Generate Q, K, V
        qkv = self.qkv_proj(x)
        qkv = qkv.reshape(B, L, 3, self.num_heads, self.head_dim)
        qkv = qkv.permute(2, 0, 3, 1, 4)
        Q, K, V = qkv[0], qkv[1], qkv[2]
        
        # Compute attention
        scores = torch.matmul(Q, K.transpose(-2, -1)) / self.scale
        
        if mask is not None:
            scores = scores.masked_fill(mask == 0, float('-inf'))
        
        attn_weights = F.softmax(scores, dim=-1)
        attn_weights = self.dropout(attn_weights)
        
        attn_output = torch.matmul(attn_weights, V)
        
        # Reshape
        attn_output = attn_output.transpose(1, 2).contiguous()
        attn_output = attn_output.reshape(B, L, D)
        attn_output = self.out_proj(attn_output)
        
        # Apply gating
        output = gate_values * attn_output + (1 - gate_values) * x
        
        return output


# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
#                    PRACTICAL EXAMPLES AND USE CASES
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

class TextClassificationWithAttention(nn.Module):
    """
    Complete text classification model using multi-head attention.
    """
    def __init__(self, vocab_size, embed_dim=256, num_heads=8, 
                 num_classes=2, max_seq_len=512, dropout=0.1):
        super(TextClassificationWithAttention, self).__init__()
        
        self.embedding = nn.Embedding(vocab_size, embed_dim, padding_idx=0)
        self.pos_encoding = nn.Parameter(torch.randn(1, max_seq_len, embed_dim))
        
        # Multi-head attention layers
        self.attention1 = MultiHeadAttention(embed_dim, num_heads, dropout)
        self.attention2 = MultiHeadAttention(embed_dim, num_heads, dropout)
        
        self.norm1 = nn.LayerNorm(embed_dim)
        self.norm2 = nn.LayerNorm(embed_dim)
        
        # Feed-forward layers
        self.ffn = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(embed_dim, embed_dim * 4),
            nn.GELU(),
            nn.Dropout(dropout),
            nn.Linear(embed_dim * 4, embed_dim),
            nn.Dropout(dropout)
        )
        
        # Classification
```python
        # Classification head
        self.classifier = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(embed_dim, embed_dim // 2),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Dropout(dropout),
            nn.Linear(embed_dim // 2, num_classes)
        )
        
        self.dropout = nn.Dropout(dropout)
        
    def forward(self, input_ids, attention_mask=None):
        """
        Args:
            input_ids: Token IDs (B, L)
            attention_mask: Attention mask (B, L)
            
        Returns:
            Classification logits (B, num_classes)
        """
        B, L = input_ids.shape
        
        # Embed tokens
        x = self.embedding(input_ids)  # (B, L, D)
        
        # Add positional encoding
        x = x + self.pos_encoding[:, :L, :]
        x = self.dropout(x)
        
        # Prepare attention mask if provided
        if attention_mask is not None:
            # Convert to attention mask format (B, 1, L, L)
            extended_mask = attention_mask.unsqueeze(1).unsqueeze(2)
            extended_mask = extended_mask.expand(B, 1, L, L)
        else:
            extended_mask = None
        
        # First attention block
        attn_out1, _ = self.attention1(x, extended_mask)
        x = self.norm1(x + attn_out1)
        
        # Feed-forward
        ffn_out = self.ffn(x)
        x = self.norm2(x + ffn_out)
        
        # Second attention block
        attn_out2, _ = self.attention2(x, extended_mask)
        x = x + attn_out2
        
        # Global average pooling
        if attention_mask is not None:
            # Mask padding tokens before pooling
            mask_expanded = attention_mask.unsqueeze(-1).expand_as(x)
            sum_embeddings = torch.sum(x * mask_expanded, dim=1)
            sum_mask = torch.clamp(mask_expanded.sum(dim=1), min=1e-9)
            pooled = sum_embeddings / sum_mask
        else:
            pooled = x.mean(dim=1)  # (B, D)
        
        # Classify
        logits = self.classifier(pooled)
        
        return logits


class ImageCaptioningWithAttention(nn.Module):
    """
    Image captioning model using cross-attention between image features
    and text embeddings.
    """
    def __init__(self, vocab_size, embed_dim=512, num_heads=8, 
                 image_feature_dim=2048, max_caption_len=50, dropout=0.1):
        super(ImageCaptioningWithAttention, self).__init__()
        
        # Image encoder projection
        self.image_proj = nn.Linear(image_feature_dim, embed_dim)
        
        # Text decoder
        self.text_embedding = nn.Embedding(vocab_size, embed_dim, padding_idx=0)
        self.pos_encoding = nn.Parameter(torch.randn(1, max_caption_len, embed_dim))
        
        # Decoder layers
        self.self_attention = MultiHeadAttention(embed_dim, num_heads, dropout)
        self.cross_attention = CrossAttention(embed_dim, embed_dim, embed_dim, 
                                             num_heads, dropout)
        
        self.norm1 = nn.LayerNorm(embed_dim)
        self.norm2 = nn.LayerNorm(embed_dim)
        self.norm3 = nn.LayerNorm(embed_dim)
        
        self.ffn = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(embed_dim, embed_dim * 4),
            nn.GELU(),
            nn.Dropout(dropout),
            nn.Linear(embed_dim * 4, embed_dim),
            nn.Dropout(dropout)
        )
        
        # Output projection
        self.output_proj = nn.Linear(embed_dim, vocab_size)
        
        self.dropout = nn.Dropout(dropout)
        
    def forward(self, image_features, caption_ids, caption_mask=None):
        """
        Args:
            image_features: Image features (B, num_regions, image_feature_dim)
            caption_ids: Caption token IDs (B, L)
            caption_mask: Optional caption mask (B, L)
            
        Returns:
            Token logits (B, L, vocab_size)
        """
        B, L = caption_ids.shape
        
        # Project image features
        image_encoded = self.image_proj(image_features)  # (B, num_regions, D)
        
        # Embed caption tokens
        text_embedded = self.text_embedding(caption_ids)  # (B, L, D)
        text_embedded = text_embedded + self.pos_encoding[:, :L, :]
        text_embedded = self.dropout(text_embedded)
        
        # Create causal mask for decoder self-attention
        causal_mask = torch.triu(
            torch.ones(L, L, device=caption_ids.device), 
            diagonal=1
        ).bool()
        causal_mask = causal_mask.unsqueeze(0).unsqueeze(0)  # (1, 1, L, L)
        
        # Decoder self-attention
        self_attn_out, _ = self.self_attention(
            text_embedded, 
            mask=(~causal_mask).float()
        )
        x = self.norm1(text_embedded + self_attn_out)
        
        # Cross-attention to image features
        cross_attn_out, attn_weights = self.cross_attention(x, image_encoded)
        x = self.norm2(x + cross_attn_out)
        
        # Feed-forward
        ffn_out = self.ffn(x)
        x = self.norm3(x + ffn_out)
        
        # Project to vocabulary
        logits = self.output_proj(x)
        
        return logits, attn_weights


class VideoActionRecognitionWithAttention(nn.Module):
    """
    Video action recognition using spatial and temporal attention.
    """
    def __init__(self, num_classes=400, feature_dim=2048, embed_dim=512,
                 num_heads=8, num_frames=16, dropout=0.1):
        super(VideoActionRecognitionWithAttention, self).__init__()
        
        self.num_frames = num_frames
        
        # Feature projection
        self.feature_proj = nn.Linear(feature_dim, embed_dim)
        
        # Temporal attention (across frames)
        self.temporal_attention = MultiHeadAttention(embed_dim, num_heads, dropout)
        
        # Spatial attention (within frames)
        self.spatial_attention = NonLocalBlock(embed_dim, embed_dim // 2)
        
        self.norm1 = nn.LayerNorm(embed_dim)
        self.norm2 = nn.LayerNorm(embed_dim)
        
        # Classification head
        self.classifier = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(embed_dim, embed_dim // 2),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Dropout(dropout),
            nn.Linear(embed_dim // 2, num_classes)
        )
        
    def forward(self, frame_features):
        """
        Args:
            frame_features: Features from each frame (B, T, H*W, feature_dim)
                           where T is number of frames
            
        Returns:
            Action class logits (B, num_classes)
        """
        B, T, N, D = frame_features.shape  # N = H*W (spatial locations)
        
        # Project features
        x = self.feature_proj(frame_features)  # (B, T, N, embed_dim)
        
        # Spatial attention within each frame
        # Reshape to process all frames together
        x_spatial = x.reshape(B * T, N, -1)  # (B*T, N, embed_dim)
        
        # For spatial attention, we need to reshape to 2D
        # Assuming square spatial dimensions
        spatial_size = int(math.sqrt(N))
        x_2d = x_spatial.reshape(B * T, -1, spatial_size, spatial_size)
        
        # Apply spatial attention (Non-Local Block)
        x_2d = self.spatial_attention(x_2d)
        
        # Reshape back
        x_spatial = x_2d.reshape(B * T, N, -1)
        x = x_spatial.reshape(B, T, N, -1)
        
        # Pool spatial dimension
        x = x.mean(dim=2)  # (B, T, embed_dim)
        
        # Temporal attention across frames
        temporal_attn_out, _ = self.temporal_attention(x)
        x = self.norm1(x + temporal_attn_out)
        
        # Global temporal pooling
        x = x.mean(dim=1)  # (B, embed_dim)
        
        # Classify
        logits = self.classifier(x)
        
        return logits


class MultiModalFusionWithAttention(nn.Module):
    """
    Multi-modal fusion using cross-attention between different modalities
    (e.g., text, image, audio).
    """
    def __init__(self, text_dim=768, image_dim=2048, audio_dim=128,
                 embed_dim=512, num_heads=8, num_classes=10, dropout=0.1):
        super(MultiModalFusionWithAttention, self).__init__()
        
        # Modality-specific projections
        self.text_proj = nn.Linear(text_dim, embed_dim)
        self.image_proj = nn.Linear(image_dim, embed_dim)
        self.audio_proj = nn.Linear(audio_dim, embed_dim)
        
        # Cross-modal attention
        self.text_to_image = CrossAttention(embed_dim, embed_dim, embed_dim, 
                                           num_heads, dropout)
        self.image_to_text = CrossAttention(embed_dim, embed_dim, embed_dim,
                                           num_heads, dropout)
        self.audio_to_both = CrossAttention(embed_dim, embed_dim, embed_dim,
                                           num_heads, dropout)
        
        # Self-attention for fusion
        self.fusion_attention = MultiHeadAttention(embed_dim, num_heads, dropout)
        
        # Gating for modality importance
        self.gate = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(embed_dim * 3, embed_dim * 3),
            nn.Sigmoid()
        )
        
        # Classification head
        self.classifier = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(embed_dim * 3, embed_dim),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Dropout(dropout),
            nn.Linear(embed_dim, num_classes)
        )
        
    def forward(self, text_features, image_features, audio_features):
        """
        Args:
            text_features: Text features (B, L_text, text_dim)
            image_features: Image features (B, L_image, image_dim)
            audio_features: Audio features (B, L_audio, audio_dim)
            
        Returns:
            Classification logits (B, num_classes)
        """
        # Project to common embedding space
        text = self.text_proj(text_features)      # (B, L_t, D)
        image = self.image_proj(image_features)   # (B, L_i, D)
        audio = self.audio_proj(audio_features)   # (B, L_a, D)
        
        # Cross-modal attention
        text_attended, _ = self.text_to_image(text, image)   # Text attends to image
        image_attended, _ = self.image_to_text(image, text)  # Image attends to text
        
        # Concatenate text and image for audio to attend to
        text_image = torch.cat([text, image], dim=1)
        audio_attended, _ = self.audio_to_both(audio, text_image)
        
        # Pool each modality
        text_pooled = text_attended.mean(dim=1)    # (B, D)
        image_pooled = image_attended.mean(dim=1)  # (B, D)
        audio_pooled = audio_attended.mean(dim=1)  # (B, D)
        
        # Concatenate all modalities
        fused = torch.cat([text_pooled, image_pooled, audio_pooled], dim=-1)  # (B, 3*D)
        
        # Apply gating for adaptive fusion
        gate_values = self.gate(fused)
        fused = fused * gate_values
        
        # Classify
        logits = self.classifier(fused)
        
        return logits

    print(f"Image Features: {image_features.shape}")
    print(f"Caption IDs: {caption_ids.shape}")
    print(f"Output Logits: {logits.shape}")
    print(f"Attention Weights: {attn_weights.shape}")
    print(f"✓ Image captioning with cross-modal attention")
    
    # 3. Video Action Recognition
    print("\n--- Video Action Recognition with Temporal Attention ---")
    batch_size, num_frames, spatial_locs, feature_dim = 2, 16, 49, 2048
    num_classes = 400
    
    video_model = VideoActionRecognitionWithAttention(
        num_classes=num_classes,
        feature_dim=feature_dim,
        embed_dim=512,
        num_heads=8,
        num_frames=num_frames
    )
    
    frame_features = torch.randn(batch_size, num_frames, spatial_locs, feature_dim)
    action_logits = video_model(frame_features)
    print(f"Frame Features: {frame_features.shape}")
    print(f"Action Logits: {action_logits.shape}")
    print(f"✓ Video action recognition with {num_classes} action classes")
    
    # 4. Multi-Modal Fusion
    print("\n--- Multi-Modal Fusion with Cross-Attention ---")
    batch_size = 4
    text_len, image_len, audio_len = 50, 49, 100
    text_dim, image_dim, audio_dim = 768, 2048, 128
    num_classes = 10
    
    multimodal_model = MultiModalFusionWithAttention(
        text_dim=text_dim,
        image_dim=image_dim,
        audio_dim=audio_dim,
        embed_dim=512,
        num_heads=8,
        num_classes=num_classes
    )
    
    text_features = torch.randn(batch_size, text_len, text_dim)
    image_features = torch.randn(batch_size, image_len, image_dim)
    audio_features = torch.randn(batch_size, audio_len, audio_dim)
    
    fusion_logits = multimodal_model(text_features, image_features, audio_features)
    print(f"Text Features: {text_features.shape}")
    print(f"Image Features: {image_features.shape}")
    print(f"Audio Features: {audio_features.shape}")
    print(f"Fusion Logits: {fusion_logits.shape}")
    print(f"✓ Multi-modal fusion with gated attention")
    
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)


def run_profiling_demo():
    """
    Demonstrate profiling capabilities.
    """
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("ATTENTION MECHANISM PROFILING")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    batch_size, seq_len, embed_dim = 4, 256, 256
    x = torch.randn(batch_size, seq_len, embed_dim)
    
    # Move to GPU if available
    device = torch.device('cuda' if torch.cuda.is_available() else 'cpu')
    x = x.to(device)
    
    print(f"\nDevice: {device}")
    print(f"Input shape: {x.shape}")
    
    # Create mechanisms to compare
    mechanisms = {
        'Multi-Head Attention': MultiHeadAttention(embed_dim, num_heads=8).to(device),
        'Linear Attention': LinearAttention(embed_dim, num_heads=8).to(device),
        'Sparse Attention': SparseAttention(embed_dim, num_heads=8, block_size=32).to(device),
    }
    
    # Profile speed
    print("\n--- Speed Profiling ---")
    for name, module in mechanisms.items():
        stats = AttentionProfiler.profile_speed(module, x, num_runs=20)
        print(f"\n{name}:")
        print(f"  Mean: {stats['mean_ms']:.3f} ms")
        print(f"  Std:  {stats['std_ms']:.3f} ms")
        print(f"  P95:  {stats['p95_ms']:.3f} ms")
    
    # Profile memory (only on CUDA)
    if torch.cuda.is_available():
        print("\n--- Memory Profiling ---")
        for name, module in mechanisms.items():
            stats = AttentionProfiler.profile_memory(module, x, num_runs=5)
            print(f"\n{name}:")
            for key, value in stats.items():
                print(f"  {key}: {value:.2f} MB")
    
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)


def run_analysis_demo():
    """
    Demonstrate attention analysis capabilities.
    """
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("ATTENTION PATTERN ANALYSIS")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    batch_size, seq_len, embed_dim = 2, 20, 64
    x = torch.randn(batch_size, seq_len, embed_dim)
    
    # Generate attention weights
    attn_module = MultiHeadAttention(embed_dim, num_heads=8)
    _, attn_weights = attn_module(x)
    
    # Analyze patterns
    print("\n--- Attention Pattern Analysis ---")
    analysis = AttentionAnalyzer.analyze_attention_pattern(attn_weights)
    
    print(f"\nAttention Statistics:")
    print(f"  Shape: {analysis['shape']}")
    print(f"  Mean: {analysis['mean']:.4f}")
    print(f"  Std: {analysis['std']:.4f}")
    print(f"  Min: {analysis['min']:.4f}")
    print(f"  Max: {analysis['max']:.4f}")
    print(f"  Entropy (mean): {analysis['entropy_mean']:.4f}")
    print(f"  Sparsity: {analysis['sparsity']:.4f}")
    print(f"  Diagonal Strength: {analysis.get('diagonal_strength', 0):.4f}")
    print(f"  Local Attention Ratio: {analysis.get('local_attention_ratio', 0):.4f}")
    print(f"  Uniformity: {analysis.get('uniformity', 0):.4f}")
    
    # Find most attended positions
    print("\n--- Top Attended Positions (First Query) ---")
    indices, values = AttentionAnalyzer.find_attended_positions(
        attn_weights[0, 0], top_k=5
    )
    for i, (idx, val) in enumerate(zip(indices[0], values[0])):
        print(f"  Rank {i+1}: Position {idx} (weight: {val:.4f})")
    
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)

def save_quick_reference():
    """
    Save a quick reference guide to a text file.
    """
    reference = """
PYTORCH ATTENTION MECHANISMS - QUICK REFERENCE
===============================================

BASIC USAGE
-----------

1. Self-Attention:
   attn = SelfAttention(embed_dim=512)
   output, weights = attn(x)

2. Multi-Head Attention:
   mha = MultiHeadAttention(embed_dim=512, num_heads=8)
   output, weights = mha(x, mask=attention_mask)

3. Cross-Attention:
   cross_attn = CrossAttention(query_dim=512, context_dim=512, 
                                embed_dim=512, num_heads=8)
   output, weights = cross_attn(query, context)

4. CBAM (for images):
   cbam = CBAM(channels=256, reduction_ratio=16)
   output = cbam(feature_maps)

5. Linear Attention (efficient):
   linear_attn = LinearAttention(embed_dim=512, num_heads=8)
   output = linear_attn(long_sequence)


COMMON PARAMETERS
-----------------
- embed_dim: Embedding dimension (256, 512, 768, 1024)
- num_heads: Number of attention heads (8, 12, 16)
- dropout: Dropout probability (0.1, 0.2)
- reduction_ratio: For channel attention (8, 16)


TROUBLESHOOTING
---------------
- Out of memory: Use sparse/linear attention, reduce batch size
- Slow training: Enable Flash Attention, use mixed precision
- NaN values: Check scaling, masking, add epsilon for stability


For complete documentation, see the main implementation file.
"""
    
    try:
        with open('attention_quick_reference.txt', 'w') as f:
            f.write(reference)
    except:

# Example training loop
class ExampleTrainingLoop:
    """
    Example training loop demonstrating how to use attention mechanisms
    in a real training scenario.
    """
    
    @staticmethod
    def train_text_classifier():
        """
        Example training loop for text classification.
        """
        print("\n" + "=" * 80)
        print("EXAMPLE: Training Text Classifier with Attention")
        print("=" * 80)
        
        # Hyperparameters
        vocab_size = 10000
        num_classes = 5
        embed_dim = 256
        num_heads = 8
        batch_size = 32
        num_epochs = 3
        learning_rate = 1e-4
        
        # Create model
        model = TextClassificationWithAttention(
            vocab_size=vocab_size,
            embed_dim=embed_dim,
            num_heads=num_heads,
            num_classes=num_classes
        )
        
        # Move to GPU if available
        device = torch.device('cuda' if torch.cuda.is_available() else 'cpu')
        model = model.to(device)
        
        print(f"\nDevice: {device}")
        print(f"Model parameters: {sum(p.numel() for p in model.parameters()):,}")
        
        # Optimizer and loss
        optimizer = torch.optim.AdamW(model.parameters(), lr=learning_rate)
        criterion = nn.CrossEntropyLoss()
        
        # Dummy data (replace with real data loader)
        def get_dummy_batch():
            input_ids = torch.randint(0, vocab_size, (batch_size, 100)).to(device)
            attention_mask = torch.ones(batch_size, 100).to(device)
            labels = torch.randint(0, num_classes, (batch_size,)).to(device)
            return input_ids, attention_mask, labels
        
        # Training loop
        print("\nTraining...")
        model.train()
        
        for epoch in range(num_epochs):
            epoch_loss = 0
            num_batches = 10  # Dummy number
            
            for batch_idx in range(num_batches):
                # Get batch
                input_ids, attention_mask, labels = get_dummy_batch()
                
                # Forward pass
                optimizer.zero_grad()
                logits = model(input_ids, attention_mask)
                loss = criterion(logits, labels)
                
                # Backward pass
                loss.backward()
                
                # Gradient clipping (optional but recommended)
                torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(model.parameters(), max_norm=1.0)
                
                optimizer.step()
                
                epoch_loss += loss.item()
                
                if batch_idx % 5 == 0:
                    print(f"  Epoch {epoch+1}/{num_epochs}, "
                          f"Batch {batch_idx}/{num_batches}, "
                          f"Loss: {loss.item():.4f}")
            
            avg_loss = epoch_loss / num_batches
            print(f"\nEpoch {epoch+1} completed. Average loss: {avg_loss:.4f}\n")
        
        print("Training completed!")
        print("=" * 80)
        
        return model
    
    @staticmethod
    def train_image_model():
        """
        Example training loop for image classification with CBAM.
        """
        print("\n" + "=" * 80)
        print("EXAMPLE: Training Image Classifier with CBAM")
        print("=" * 80)
        
        # Simple CNN with CBAM
        class SimpleCNNWithCBAM(nn.Module):
            def __init__(self, num_classes=10):
                super(SimpleCNNWithCBAM, self).__init__()
                
                self.features = nn.Sequential(
                    nn.Conv2d(3, 64, 3, padding=1),
                    nn.BatchNorm2d(64),
                    nn.ReLU(),
                    nn.MaxPool2d(2),
                    
                    nn.Conv2d(64, 128, 3, padding=1),
                    nn.BatchNorm2d(128),
                    nn.ReLU(),
                    CBAM(128, reduction_ratio=16),
                    nn.MaxPool2d(2),
                    
                    nn.Conv2d(128, 256, 3, padding=1),
                    nn.BatchNorm2d(256),
                    nn.ReLU(),
                    CBAM(256, reduction_ratio=16),
                    nn.MaxPool2d(2),
                )
                
                self.classifier = nn.Sequential(
                    nn.AdaptiveAvgPool2d(1),
                    nn.Flatten(),
                    nn.Linear(256, num_classes)
                )
            
            def forward(self, x):
                x = self.features(x)
                x = self.classifier(x)
                return x
        
        # Create model
        model = SimpleCNNWithCBAM(num_classes=10)
        device = torch.device('cuda' if torch.cuda.is_available() else 'cpu')
        model = model.to(device)
        
        print(f"\nDevice: {device}")
        print(f"Model parameters: {sum(p.numel() for p in model.parameters()):,}")
        
        # Optimizer and loss
        optimizer = torch.optim.Adam(model.parameters(), lr=1e-3)
        criterion = nn.CrossEntropyLoss()
        
        # Dummy data
        batch_size = 16
        num_batches = 5
        
        print("\nTraining...")
        model.train()
        
        for batch_idx in range(num_batches):
            # Dummy batch
            images = torch.randn(batch_size, 3, 32, 32).to(device)
            labels = torch.randint(0, 10, (batch_size,)).to(device)
            
            # Forward pass
            optimizer.zero_grad()
            logits = model(images)
            loss = criterion(logits, labels)
            
            # Backward pass
            loss.backward()
            optimizer.step()
            
            print(f"  Batch {batch_idx+1}/{num_batches}, Loss: {loss.item():.4f}")
        
        print("\nTraining completed!")
        print("=" * 80)
        
        return model

def export_model_example():
    """
    Example of how to save and load models with attention mechanisms.
    """
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("MODEL EXPORT AND LOADING EXAMPLE")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    # Create a model
    model = TextClassificationWithAttention(
        vocab_size=10000,
        embed_dim=256,
        num_heads=8,
        num_classes=5
    )
    
    print("\n1. Saving model...")
    
    # Save entire model
    torch.save(model, 'attention_model_full.pth')
    print("   ✓ Full model saved to 'attention_model_full.pth'")
    
    # Save only state dict (recommended)
    torch.save(model.state_dict(), 'attention_model_state.pth')
    print("   ✓ State dict saved to 'attention_model_state.pth'")
    
    # Save checkpoint with optimizer state
    checkpoint = {
        'model_state_dict': model.state_dict(),
        'optimizer_state_dict': torch.optim.Adam(model.parameters()).state_dict(),
        'epoch': 10,
        'loss': 0.5,
    }
    torch.save(checkpoint, 'attention_checkpoint.pth')
    print("   ✓ Checkpoint saved to 'attention_checkpoint.pth'")
    
    print("\n2. Loading model...")
    
    # Load full model
    loaded_model = torch.load('attention_model_full.pth')
    print("   ✓ Full model loaded")
    
    # Load state dict
    new_model = TextClassificationWithAttention(
        vocab_size=10000,
        embed_dim=256,
        num_heads=8,
        num_classes=5
    )
    new_model.load_state_dict(torch.load('attention_model_state.pth'))
    print("   ✓ State dict loaded")
    
    # Load checkpoint
    checkpoint = torch.load('attention_checkpoint.pth')
    new_model.load_state_dict(checkpoint['model_state_dict'])
    print(f"   ✓ Checkpoint loaded (epoch {checkpoint['epoch']}, loss {checkpoint['loss']})")
    
    # Clean up
    import os
    for file in ['attention_model_full.pth', 'attention_model_state.pth', 
                 'attention_checkpoint.pth']:
        try:
            os.remove(file)
        except:
            pass
    
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)

## 1. Encoder-Only Transformer (BERT-style)

```python
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F
from typing import Optional, Tuple
import math

class MultiHeadAttention(nn.Module):
    """Multi-Head Attention mechanism with scaled dot-product attention."""
    
    def __init__(self, d_model: int, num_heads: int, dropout: float = 0.1):
        super().__init__()
        assert d_model % num_heads == 0, "d_model must be divisible by num_heads"
        
        self.d_model = d_model
        self.num_heads = num_heads
        self.d_k = d_model // num_heads
        
        # Linear projections for Q, K, V
        self.W_q = nn.Linear(d_model, d_model)
        self.W_k = nn.Linear(d_model, d_model)
        self.W_v = nn.Linear(d_model, d_model)
        self.W_o = nn.Linear(d_model, d_model)
        
        self.dropout = nn.Dropout(dropout)
        
    def forward(self, query: torch.Tensor, key: torch.Tensor, value: torch.Tensor,
                mask: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None) -> Tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
        batch_size = query.size(0)
        
        # Linear projections and reshape for multi-head attention
        Q = self.W_q(query).view(batch_size, -1, self.num_heads, self.d_k).transpose(1, 2)
        K = self.W_k(key).view(batch_size, -1, self.num_heads, self.d_k).transpose(1, 2)
        V = self.W_v(value).view(batch_size, -1, self.num_heads, self.d_k).transpose(1, 2)
        
        # Scaled dot-product attention
        scores = torch.matmul(Q, K.transpose(-2, -1)) / math.sqrt(self.d_k)
        
        if mask is not None:
            scores = scores.masked_fill(mask == 0, -1e9)
        
        attention_weights = F.softmax(scores, dim=-1)
        attention_weights = self.dropout(attention_weights)
        
        # Apply attention to values
        context = torch.matmul(attention_weights, V)
        
        # Concatenate heads and apply output projection
        context = context.transpose(1, 2).contiguous().view(batch_size, -1, self.d_model)
        output = self.W_o(context)
        
        return output, attention_weights


class FeedForward(nn.Module):
    """Position-wise Feed-Forward Network."""
    
    def __init__(self, d_model: int, d_ff: int, dropout: float = 0.1):
        super().__init__()
        self.linear1 = nn.Linear(d_model, d_ff)
        self.linear2 = nn.Linear(d_ff, d_model)
        self.dropout = nn.Dropout(dropout)
        
    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        return self.linear2(self.dropout(F.gelu(self.linear1(x))))


class EncoderLayer(nn.Module):
    """Single Transformer Encoder Layer."""
    
    def __init__(self, d_model: int, num_heads: int, d_ff: int, dropout: float = 0.1):
        super().__init__()
        self.self_attention = MultiHeadAttention(d_model, num_heads, dropout)
        self.feed_forward = FeedForward(d_model, d_ff, dropout)
        self.norm1 = nn.LayerNorm(d_model)
        self.norm2 = nn.LayerNorm(d_model)
        self.dropout = nn.Dropout(dropout)
        
    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor, mask: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None) -> torch.Tensor:
        # Self-attention with residual connection
        attn_output, _ = self.self_attention(x, x, x, mask)
        x = self.norm1(x + self.dropout(attn_output))
        
        # Feed-forward with residual connection
        ff_output = self.feed_forward(x)
        x = self.norm2(x + self.dropout(ff_output))
        
        return x


class EncoderOnlyTransformer(nn.Module):
    """
    Encoder-Only Transformer (BERT-style).
    Used for tasks like classification, NER, and masked language modeling.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, vocab_size: int, d_model: int = 512, num_heads: int = 8,
                 num_layers: int = 6, d_ff: int = 2048, max_seq_len: int = 512,
                 dropout: float = 0.1, num_classes: int = 2):
        super().__init__()
        
        self.d_model = d_model
        
        # Embeddings
        self.token_embedding = nn.Embedding(vocab_size, d_model)
        self.position_embedding = nn.Embedding(max_seq_len, d_model)
        
        # Encoder layers
        self.encoder_layers = nn.ModuleList([
            EncoderLayer(d_model, num_heads, d_ff, dropout)
            for _ in range(num_layers)
        ])
        
        self.dropout = nn.Dropout(dropout)
        
        # Classification head
        self.classifier = nn.Linear(d_model, num_classes)
        
        self._init_weights()
        
    def _init_weights(self):
        """Initialize weights using Xavier uniform initialization."""
        for p in self.parameters():
            if p.dim() > 1:
                nn.init.xavier_uniform_(p)
    
    def forward(self, input_ids: torch.Tensor, 
                attention_mask: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None) -> torch.Tensor:
        batch_size, seq_len = input_ids.size()
        
        # Create position indices
        positions = torch.arange(seq_len, device=input_ids.device).unsqueeze(0).expand(batch_size, -1)
        
        # Embeddings
        x = self.token_embedding(input_ids) + self.position_embedding(positions)
        x = self.dropout(x)
        
        # Prepare attention mask
        if attention_mask is not None:
            attention_mask = attention_mask.unsqueeze(1).unsqueeze(2)
        
        # Pass through encoder layers
        for layer in self.encoder_layers:
            x = layer(x, attention_mask)
        
        # Use [CLS] token (first token) for classification
        cls_output = x[:, 0]
        logits = self.classifier(cls_output)
        
        return logits


# Example usage
if __name__ == "__main__":

    vocab_size = 30000
    batch_size = 8

    # Forward pass
    output = model(input_ids, attention_mask)
    print(f"Encoder-Only Output shape: {output.shape}")  # [batch_size, num_classes]

## 2. Decoder-Only Transformer (GPT-style)

```python
class DecoderLayer(nn.Module):
    """Single Transformer Decoder Layer with causal masking."""
    
    def __init__(self, d_model: int, num_heads: int, d_ff: int, dropout: float = 0.1):
        super().__init__()
        self.self_attention = MultiHeadAttention(d_model, num_heads, dropout)
        self.feed_forward = FeedForward(d_model, d_ff, dropout)
        self.norm1 = nn.LayerNorm(d_model)
        self.norm2 = nn.LayerNorm(d_model)
        self.dropout = nn.Dropout(dropout)
        
    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor, causal_mask: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        # Masked self-attention with residual connection
        attn_output, _ = self.self_attention(x, x, x, causal_mask)
        x = self.norm1(x + self.dropout(attn_output))
        
        # Feed-forward with residual connection
        ff_output = self.feed_forward(x)
        x = self.norm2(x + self.dropout(ff_output))
        
        return x


class DecoderOnlyTransformer(nn.Module):
    """
    Decoder-Only Transformer (GPT-style).
    Used for autoregressive language modeling and text generation.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, vocab_size: int, d_model: int = 768, num_heads: int = 12,
                 num_layers: int = 12, d_ff: int = 3072, max_seq_len: int = 1024,
                 dropout: float = 0.1):
        super().__init__()
        
        self.d_model = d_model
        self.max_seq_len = max_seq_len
        
        # Embeddings
        self.token_embedding = nn.Embedding(vocab_size, d_model)
        self.position_embedding = nn.Embedding(max_seq_len, d_model)
        
        # Decoder layers
        self.decoder_layers = nn.ModuleList([
            DecoderLayer(d_model, num_heads, d_ff, dropout)
            for _ in range(num_layers)
        ])
        
        self.dropout = nn.Dropout(dropout)
        self.norm = nn.LayerNorm(d_model)
        
        # Language modeling head
        self.lm_head = nn.Linear(d_model, vocab_size, bias=False)
        
        # Tie weights between embedding and lm_head
        self.lm_head.weight = self.token_embedding.weight
        
        self._init_weights()
        
    def _init_weights(self):
        """Initialize weights."""
        for p in self.parameters():
            if p.dim() > 1:
                nn.init.xavier_uniform_(p)
    
    def _create_causal_mask(self, seq_len: int, device: torch.device) -> torch.Tensor:
        """Create causal mask to prevent attending to future tokens."""
        mask = torch.tril(torch.ones(seq_len, seq_len, device=device))
        return mask.unsqueeze(0).unsqueeze(0)  # [1, 1, seq_len, seq_len]
    
    def forward(self, input_ids: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        batch_size, seq_len = input_ids.size()
        device = input_ids.device
        
        # Create position indices
        positions = torch.arange(seq_len, device=device).unsqueeze(0).expand(batch_size, -1)
        
        # Embeddings
        x = self.token_embedding(input_ids) + self.position_embedding(positions)
        x = self.dropout(x)
        
        # Create causal mask
        causal_mask = self._create_causal_mask(seq_len, device)
        
        # Pass through decoder layers
        for layer in self.decoder_layers:
            x = layer(x, causal_mask)
        
        x = self.norm(x)
        
        # Project to vocabulary
        logits = self.lm_head(x)
        
        return logits
    
    @torch.no_grad()
    def generate(self, input_ids: torch.Tensor, max_new_tokens: int = 50,
                 temperature: float = 1.0, top_k: Optional[int] = None) -> torch.Tensor:
        """Generate text autoregressively."""
        self.eval()
        
        for _ in range(max_new_tokens):
            # Crop context if needed
            idx_cond = input_ids if input_ids.size(1) <= self.max_seq_len else input_ids[:, -self.max_seq_len:]
            
            # Forward pass
            logits = self(idx_cond)
            logits = logits[:, -1, :] / temperature
            
            # Optional top-k sampling
            if top_k is not None:
                v, _ = torch.topk(logits, min(top_k, logits.size(-1)))
                logits[logits < v[:, [-1]]] = -float('Inf')
            
            # Sample from distribution
            probs = F.softmax(logits, dim=-1)
            idx_next = torch.multinomial(probs, num_samples=1)
            
            # Append to sequence
            input_ids = torch.cat([input_ids, idx_next], dim=1)
        
        return input_ids


# Example usage
if __name__ == "__main__":
    vocab_size = 50000
    batch_size = 4
    seq_len = 256
    
    model = DecoderOnlyTransformer(
        vocab_size=vocab_size,
        d_model=768,
        num_heads=12,
        num_layers=12,
        d_ff=3072
    )
    
    input_ids = torch.randint(0, vocab_size, (batch_size, seq_len))
    output = model(input_ids)
    print(f"Decoder-Only Output shape: {output.shape}")  # [batch_size, seq_len, vocab_size]
    
    # Generation example
    prompt = torch.randint(0, vocab_size, (1, 10))
    generated = model.generate(prompt, max_new_tokens=50, temperature=0.8, top_k=40)
    print(f"Generated sequence shape: {generated.shape}")

## 3. Encoder-Decoder Transformer (T5-style)

```python
class EncoderDecoderAttention(nn.Module):
    """Cross-attention between encoder and decoder."""
    
    def __init__(self, d_model: int, num_heads: int, dropout: float = 0.1):
        super().__init__()
        self.attention = MultiHeadAttention(d_model, num_heads, dropout)
        
    def forward(self, decoder_hidden: torch.Tensor, encoder_output: torch.Tensor,
                encoder_mask: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None) -> Tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
        return self.attention(decoder_hidden, encoder_output, encoder_output, encoder_mask)


class EncoderDecoderLayer(nn.Module):
    """Decoder layer with cross-attention to encoder outputs."""
    
    def __init__(self, d_model: int, num_heads: int, d_ff: int, dropout: float = 0.1):
        super().__init__()
        self.self_attention = MultiHeadAttention(
```python
        self.self_attention = MultiHeadAttention(d_model, num_heads, dropout)
        self.cross_attention = EncoderDecoderAttention(d_model, num_heads, dropout)
        self.feed_forward = FeedForward(d_model, d_ff, dropout)
        
        self.norm1 = nn.LayerNorm(d_model)
        self.norm2 = nn.LayerNorm(d_model)
        self.norm3 = nn.LayerNorm(d_model)
        self.dropout = nn.Dropout(dropout)
        
    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor, encoder_output: torch.Tensor,
                causal_mask: torch.Tensor, encoder_mask: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None) -> torch.Tensor:
        # Self-attention with causal masking
        attn_output, _ = self.self_attention(x, x, x, causal_mask)
        x = self.norm1(x + self.dropout(attn_output))
        
        # Cross-attention to encoder outputs
        cross_attn_output, _ = self.cross_attention(x, encoder_output, encoder_mask)
        x = self.norm2(x + self.dropout(cross_attn_output))
        
        # Feed-forward
        ff_output = self.feed_forward(x)
        x = self.norm3(x + self.dropout(ff_output))
        
        return x


class EncoderDecoderTransformer(nn.Module):
    """
    Encoder-Decoder Transformer (T5/BART-style).
    Used for sequence-to-sequence tasks like translation, summarization.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, src_vocab_size: int, tgt_vocab_size: int,
                 d_model: int = 512, num_heads: int = 8,
                 num_encoder_layers: int = 6, num_decoder_layers: int = 6,
                 d_ff: int = 2048, max_seq_len: int = 512, dropout: float = 0.1):
        super().__init__()
        
        self.d_model = d_model
        self.max_seq_len = max_seq_len
        
        # Encoder embeddings
        self.encoder_embedding = nn.Embedding(src_vocab_size, d_model)
        self.encoder_pos_embedding = nn.Embedding(max_seq_len, d_model)
        
        # Decoder embeddings
        self.decoder_embedding = nn.Embedding(tgt_vocab_size, d_model)
        self.decoder_pos_embedding = nn.Embedding(max_seq_len, d_model)
        
        # Encoder
        self.encoder_layers = nn.ModuleList([
            EncoderLayer(d_model, num_heads, d_ff, dropout)
            for _ in range(num_encoder_layers)
        ])
        
        # Decoder
        self.decoder_layers = nn.ModuleList([
            EncoderDecoderLayer(d_model, num_heads, d_ff, dropout)
            for _ in range(num_decoder_layers)
        ])
        
        self.dropout = nn.Dropout(dropout)
        self.norm = nn.LayerNorm(d_model)
        
        # Output projection
        self.output_projection = nn.Linear(d_model, tgt_vocab_size)
        
        self._init_weights()
        
    def _init_weights(self):
        """Initialize weights."""
        for p in self.parameters():
            if p.dim() > 1:
                nn.init.xavier_uniform_(p)
    
    def _create_causal_mask(self, seq_len: int, device: torch.device) -> torch.Tensor:
        """Create causal mask for decoder."""
        mask = torch.tril(torch.ones(seq_len, seq_len, device=device))
        return mask.unsqueeze(0).unsqueeze(0)
    
    def encode(self, src_ids: torch.Tensor, 
               src_mask: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None) -> torch.Tensor:
        """Encode source sequence."""
        batch_size, seq_len = src_ids.size()
        device = src_ids.device
        
        # Position indices
        positions = torch.arange(seq_len, device=device).unsqueeze(0).expand(batch_size, -1)
        
        # Embeddings
        x = self.encoder_embedding(src_ids) + self.encoder_pos_embedding(positions)
        x = self.dropout(x)
        
        # Prepare encoder mask
        if src_mask is not None:
            src_mask = src_mask.unsqueeze(1).unsqueeze(2)
        
        # Pass through encoder layers
        for layer in self.encoder_layers:
            x = layer(x, src_mask)
        
        return x
    
    def decode(self, tgt_ids: torch.Tensor, encoder_output: torch.Tensor,
               src_mask: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None) -> torch.Tensor:
        """Decode target sequence given encoder outputs."""
        batch_size, seq_len = tgt_ids.size()
        device = tgt_ids.device
        
        # Position indices
        positions = torch.arange(seq_len, device=device).unsqueeze(0).expand(batch_size, -1)
        
        # Embeddings
        x = self.decoder_embedding(tgt_ids) + self.decoder_pos_embedding(positions)
        x = self.dropout(x)
        
        # Create causal mask
        causal_mask = self._create_causal_mask(seq_len, device)
        
        # Prepare encoder mask
        if src_mask is not None:
            src_mask = src_mask.unsqueeze(1).unsqueeze(2)
        
        # Pass through decoder layers
        for layer in self.decoder_layers:
            x = layer(x, encoder_output, causal_mask, src_mask)
        
        x = self.norm(x)
        
        return x
    
    def forward(self, src_ids: torch.Tensor, tgt_ids: torch.Tensor,
                src_mask: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
                tgt_mask: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None) -> torch.Tensor:
        """Forward pass through encoder-decoder."""
        # Encode
        encoder_output = self.encode(src_ids, src_mask)
        
        # Decode
        decoder_output = self.decode(tgt_ids, encoder_output, src_mask)
        
        # Project to vocabulary
        logits = self.output_projection(decoder_output)
        
        return logits
    
    @torch.no_grad()
    def generate(self, src_ids: torch.Tensor, src_mask: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
                 max_len: int = 100, start_token: int = 1, end_token: int = 2) -> torch.Tensor:
        """Generate target sequence using greedy decoding."""
        self.eval()
        batch_size = src_ids.size(0)
        device = src_ids.device
        
        # Encode source
        encoder_output = self.encode(src_ids, src_mask)
        
        # Initialize with start token
        tgt_ids = torch.full((batch_size, 1), start_token, dtype=torch.long, device=device)
        
        for _ in range(max_len - 1):
            # Decode
            decoder_output = self.decode(tgt_ids, encoder_output, src_mask)
            
            # Get next token prediction
            next_token_logits = self.output_projection(decoder_output[:, -1, :])
            next_token = next_token_logits.argmax(dim=-1, keepdim=True)
            
            # Append to sequence
            tgt_ids = torch.cat([tgt_ids, next_token], dim=1)
            
            # Stop if all sequences have generated end token
            if (next_token == end_token).all():
                break
        
        return tgt_ids


# Example usage
if __name__ == "__main__":
    src_vocab_size = 30000
    tgt_vocab_size = 30000
    batch_size = 8
    src_len = 64
    tgt_len = 64
    
    model = EncoderDecoderTransformer(
        src_vocab_size=src_vocab_size,
        tgt_vocab_size=tgt_vocab_size,
        d_model=512,
        num_heads=8,
        num_encoder_layers=6,
        num_decoder_layers=6,
        d_ff=2048
    )
    
    src_ids = torch.randint(0, src_vocab_size, (batch_size, src_len))
    tgt_ids = torch.randint(0, tgt_vocab_size, (batch_size, tgt_len))
    src_mask = torch.ones(batch_size, src_len)
    
    output = model(src_ids, tgt_ids, src_mask)
    print(f"Encoder-Decoder Output shape: {output.shape}")  # [batch_size, tgt_len, tgt_vocab_size]
    
    # Generation example
    generated = model.generate(src_ids[:1], src_mask[:1], max_len=50)
    print(f"Generated sequence shape: {generated.shape}")

## 4. Vision Transformer (ViT)

```python
class PatchEmbedding(nn.Module):
    """
    Split image into patches and embed them.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, img_size: int = 224, patch_size: int = 16, 
                 in_channels: int = 3, embed_dim: int = 768):
        super().__init__()
        self.img_size = img_size
        self.patch_size = patch_size
        self.n_patches = (img_size // patch_size) ** 2
        
        # Convolutional layer to create patch embeddings
        self.projection = nn.Conv2d(
            in_channels, embed_dim, 
            kernel_size=patch_size, 
            stride=patch_size
        )
        
    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        # x: [batch_size, channels, height, width]
        x = self.projection(x)  # [batch_size, embed_dim, n_patches**0.5, n_patches**0.5]
        x = x.flatten(2)  # [batch_size, embed_dim, n_patches]
        x = x.transpose(1, 2)  # [batch_size, n_patches, embed_dim]
        return x


class VisionTransformer(nn.Module):
    """
    Vision Transformer (ViT) for image classification.
    Treats images as sequences of patches.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, img_size: int = 224, patch_size: int = 16, 
                 in_channels: int = 3, num_classes: int = 1000,
                 d_model: int = 768, num_heads: int = 12, num_layers: int = 12,
                 d_ff: int = 3072, dropout: float = 0.1):
        super().__init__()
        
        self.patch_embedding = PatchEmbedding(img_size, patch_size, in_channels, d_model)
        n_patches = self.patch_embedding.n_patches
        
        # CLS token
        self.cls_token = nn.Parameter(torch.randn(1, 1, d_model))
        
        # Position embeddings (including CLS token)
        self.position_embedding = nn.Parameter(torch.randn(1, n_patches + 1, d_model))
        
        # Transformer encoder
        self.encoder_layers = nn.ModuleList([
            EncoderLayer(d_model, num_heads, d_ff, dropout)
            for _ in range(num_layers)
        ])
        
        self.dropout = nn.Dropout(dropout)
        self.norm = nn.LayerNorm(d_model)
        
        # Classification head
        self.mlp_head = nn.Sequential(
            nn.LayerNorm(d_model),
            nn.Linear(d_model, num_classes)
        )
        
        self._init_weights()
        
    def _init_weights(self):
        """Initialize weights."""
        # Initialize patch embedding like a linear layer
        w = self.patch_embedding.projection.weight.data
        nn.init.xavier_uniform_(w.view([w.shape[0], -1]))
        
        # Initialize other parameters
        nn.init.normal_(self.cls_token, std=0.02)
        nn.init.normal_(self.position_embedding, std=0.02)
        
        for module in self.modules():
            if isinstance(module, nn.Linear):
                nn.init.xavier_uniform_(module.weight)
                if module.bias is not None:
                    nn.init.zeros_(module.bias)
            elif isinstance(module, nn.LayerNorm):
                nn.init.ones_(module.weight)
                nn.init.zeros_(module.bias)
    
    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        batch_size = x.size(0)
        
        # Create patch embeddings
        x = self.patch_embedding(x)  # [batch_size, n_patches, d_model]
        
        # Prepend CLS token
        cls_tokens = self.cls_token.expand(batch_size, -1, -1)
        x = torch.cat([cls_tokens, x], dim=1)  # [batch_size, n_patches+1, d_model]
        
        # Add position embeddings
        x = x + self.position_embedding
        x = self.dropout(x)
        
        # Pass through transformer encoder
        for layer in self.encoder_layers:
            x = layer(x)
        
        x = self.norm(x)
        
        # Use CLS token for classification
        cls_output = x[:, 0]
        logits = self.mlp_head(cls_output)
        
        return logits


# Example usage
if __name__ == "__main__":
    batch_size = 4
    img_size = 224
    in_channels = 3
    num_classes = 1000
    
    model = VisionTransformer(
        img_size=img_size,
        patch_size=16,
        in_channels=in_channels,
        num_classes=num_classes,
        d_model=768,
        num_heads=12,
        num_layers=12,
        d_ff=3072
    )
    
    images = torch.randn(batch_size, in_channels, img_size, img_size)
    output = model(images)
    print(f"Vision Transformer Output shape: {output.shape}")  # [batch_size, num_classes]
